stimulus.text: Among the highlights of the city library's spring exhibition is a collection of botanical illustrations that, along with several handwritten journals from the same estate, ___ on display in the east wing through the end of the month.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
rationale: The blank needs a finite verb for the relative clause beginning with "that." The subject of that clause is "collection" (via the relative pronoun "that"), which is singular; the phrase "along with several handwritten journals from the same estate" interrupts but does not change the number of the subject. The time frame — an exhibition running "through the end of the month" — calls for the present tense. The singular present form "is" satisfies both signals. Choice B, "are," agrees with the nearer plural noun "journals," but that noun is the object of a prepositional phrase, not the subject — the classic decoy-noun misparse. Choice C, "being," is a participle, so the relative clause would contain no finite verb, leaving the sentence a fragment. Choice A, "were," is both plural and past tense; even read as a tense choice alone, it clashes with the ongoing present time frame established by "through the end of the month."
